meta.scene_summary: We're busy building the future, but we still haven't figured out how to stop our TVs from eavesdropping or our servers from burning the house down.

cooking.headline: Nvidia just handed OpenAI the 'AGI' trophy while selling the stadium
cooking.summary: Jensen Huang officially declared AGI has arrived, which is a convenient take when you're the one supplying all the chips for the party. It's like a construction company congratulating a homeowner on finishing their house, right before sending the invoice for the bricks.
cooking.plain_english: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang publicly stated that artificial general intelligence has been achieved and congratulated OpenAI on the milestone.

cooking.headline: Switzerland is breaking up with Microsoft for 3,000 computers
cooking.summary: The Swiss government is replacing Microsoft on thousands of machines, proving that even countries eventually get tired of the enterprise subscription lifecycle. It's the digital equivalent of moving out of your parents' house to finally have control over your own thermostat.
cooking.plain_english: The Swiss federal government has initiated a pilot program to replace Microsoft software with alternative solutions on 3,000 of its computers.

cooking.headline: vLLM adds AMD support, finally letting your GPUs touch grass
cooking.summary: vLLM is bringing speculative decoding to AMD hardware, effectively ending the Nvidia monopoly on your local LLM experiments. It's like finally being allowed to use the fancy gym equipment that's been sitting in the corner collecting dust.
cooking.plain_english: The vLLM software library now supports accelerated AI model performance on AMD graphics cards.

cooking.headline: Tottenham Hotspur saved 85% on licensing, proving even IT can score
cooking.summary: Tottenham Hotspur managed to slash their VMware licensing fees by 85% just by migrating to a different stack. It turns out the biggest win for the club this season happened in the server room, not on the pitch.
cooking.plain_english: Tottenham Hotspur significantly reduced its annual software costs by migrating away from its existing virtualization platform.

cooking.headline: Sandboxing your AI agents because you don't trust them not to nuke your root directory
cooking.summary: Trail of Bits released a tool to run AI code agents in isolated VMs, effectively giving your LLM its own personal padded cell. It turns out that letting an AI execute arbitrary shell commands is a lot like giving a toddler a chainsaw and hoping they only use it for arts and crafts.
cooking.plain_english: A new tool allows developers to run AI-generated code inside secure, isolated virtual environments to prevent potential security risks.

cooked.headline: The 'Federation' just learned that shared keys are basically a communal wallet
cooked.summary: The Liquid Federation lost $320 million because apparently, keeping a massive pile of Bitcoin in one place is still a security strategy. It's the digital equivalent of leaving the bank vault door propped open with a brick and acting surprised when someone walks out with the cash.
cooked.plain_english: Hackers stole approximately 4,000 Bitcoin worth about $320 million from a digital wallet managed by the Liquid Federation.

cooked.headline: LG TVs are listening to your silence even when the screen is off
cooked.summary: LG smart TVs are reportedly logging audio and snooping on your local network while you aren't even watching. It turns out the 'smart' in smart TV mostly refers to how effectively it functions as an undercover roommate.
cooked.plain_english: LG smart televisions have been found recording audio and scanning connected home devices even when the displays are powered off.

cooked.headline: OpenAI is putting your productivity back on a leash
cooked.summary: OpenAI is bringing back the 5-hour limit for Plus users, proving that unlimited intelligence is actually just a trial subscription. It turns out the future of AI is just getting told to go touch grass once you've hit your quota.
cooked.plain_english: OpenAI has reinstated a limit that restricts paid users to five hours of usage within a specific timeframe.

cooked.headline: Flock AI surveillance is getting a bipartisan 'no thank you'
cooked.summary: Flock Safety's surveillance tech is currently undergoing a vibe check from Republicans who aren't exactly fans of being watched. It turns out that 'law and order' loses its appeal the moment the government starts using the same cameras to watch you.
cooked.plain_english: United States Republican lawmakers are expressing significant opposition to the use of Flock Safety's AI-powered surveillance cameras.

cooked.headline: Smartphone manufacturers treat EU repairability laws like a 'suggested' syllabus
cooked.summary: EU regulators are finding that phone makers are ignoring repairability mandates with the same enthusiasm a student gives a group project they plan to drop. It's almost as if shipping a device that's impossible to open is a feature, not a bug, for their business model.
cooked.plain_english: Major smartphone manufacturers are failing to meet new European Union requirements that mandate easier device repairs for consumers.
